history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: seq 294 in this dataset ('Takhteshwar Temple', file 294.json, id 'takhteshwar-temple-bhavnagar') is the same temple - one of the two records should be merged or removed. Shree Takhteshwar Temple stands on a hillock in the centre of Bhavnagar city. Built entirely of white marble in the Gujarati style on the orders of Maharaja Takhtsinhji (one of Bhavnagar's most influential rulers) and completed in 1893, it is named after him ('Takht' = throne, 'Ishwar' = God). The shrine has an 18-pillared mandapa and a shikhara over the sanctum housing a three-eyed Shiva idol; the marble courtyard holds a Nandi statue and hand-drawn sacred symbols. The hilltop commands a panoramic view over Bhavnagar city to the Gulf of Khambhat (Gulf of Cambay), making it one of the city's landmarks. town_description: Bhavnagar is a major port city and former princely state capital in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the western shore of the Gulf of Khambhat. Founded in 1724 by Bhavsinhji Gohil, it is known for the Takhteshwar Temple hill, Nilambag Palace, Gaurishankar Lake and the nearby sea temples of Koliyak and Talaja, as well as the Blackbuck National Park at Velavadar. It is well connected by rail, road and a domestic airport.
